title: Five times too small to see: cell theory, scale, and emergence

objectives.statement: Compute the smallest separation an unaided eye resolves from a stated angular limit and viewing distance, compare that threshold with a stated cell size as a factor, and decide from the comparison which instrument a stated biological question requires.

State what cell theory asserts with its cellular-lineage boundary, name observations that would count against two of its propositions, and explain why a scientific theory is a broad, evidence-supported and revisable explanation rather than an untested guess or a promoted hypothesis.

Distinguish a property belonging to the organisation of a tissue from a property of any single cell within it, and defend the classification by applying the two-part test rather than by asserting the category.
